SUMMARY\n\n### Technical Context\n\n| Aspect | Value |\n|--------|-------|\n| **Language/Stack** | Markdown-first spec documentation for an automation-focused AI system |\n| **Framework** | System Spec Kit Level 3 structure |\n| **Storage** | `.opencode/specs/00--ai-systems-non-dev/002-sales-communication-flows/001-initial-creation/` |\n| **Testing** | `validate.sh --strict` and `validate.sh --verbose` |\n\n### Overview\nThis phase creates the initial Sales Ops planning package that defines how the automation system should be structured, reviewed, and extended. The work focuses on documentation architecture, quality controls, and cross-document consistency rather than shipping runnable Google Apps Script code.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:summary -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:quality-gates -->\n## 2. QUALITY GATES\n\n### Definition of Ready\n- [x] Problem statement is documented in `spec.md`\n- [x] Parent-child phase links exist\n- [x] Required Level 3 files are present\n\n### Definition of Done\n- [ ] All Level 3 documents validate with 0 errors\n- [ ] Cross-document references resolve inside the assigned subtree\n- [ ] Safety, export, and command-routing rules are synchronized across spec documents\n<!-- /ANCHOR:quality-gates -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:architecture -->\n## 3. ARCHITECTURE\n\n### Pattern\nDocumentation architecture with a parent phase shell and one Level 3 child phase bundle.\n\n### Key Components\n- **Phase spec**: Defines system boundaries, requirements, risks, and user stories\n- **Implementation plan**: Defines the structure, sequencing, and validation strategy\n- **Tasks**: Tracks the work needed to assemble and verify the Sales Ops package\n- **Checklist**: Captures release-style verification gates with evidence expectations\n- **Decision record**: Documents foundational architecture choices for the automation system\n\n### Data Flow\nThe parent spec provides the phase tree entry point. The child phase spec defines the initial system requirements, the plan turns those requirements into execution stages, the tasks file tracks completion, and the checklist and ADRs validate that the resulting package is coherent and safe to extend.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:architecture -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:phases -->\n## 4. IMPLEMENTATION PHASES\n\n### Phase 1: Setup\n- [ ] Normalize the Level 3 document structure\n- [ ] Restore required anchors, headers, and level declarations\n- [ ] Confirm parent-child references resolve\n\n### Phase 2: Core Implementation\n- [ ] Capture the Sales Ops system boundary and operating model\n- [ ] Document quality controls, command routing, dependencies, and export rules\n- [ ] Consolidate architecture decisions into ADR format\n\n### Phase 3: Verification\n- [ ] Re-run strict validation after each file update\n- [ ] Repair remaining integrity issues\n- [ ] Confirm the subtree reports 0 validation errors\n<!-- /ANCHOR:phases -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:testing -->\n## 5. TESTING STRATEGY\n\n| Test Type | Scope | Tools |\n|-----------|-------|-------|\n| Structural validation | Anchors, headers, level declarations, file presence | `validate.sh --strict` |\n| Recursive validation | Parent plus child phase consistency | `validate.sh --verbose` |\n| Manual review | Accuracy of Sales Ops positioning and document cross-links | File inspection |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:testing -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:dependencies -->\n## 6. DEPENDENCIES\n\n| Dependency | Type | Status | Impact if Blocked |\n|------------|------|--------|-------------------|\n| Parent phase shell | Internal | Green | Child metadata and recursive validation lose their entry point |\n| Shared Brand reference | External to subtree | Green | Sales terminology and positioning become less grounded |\n| Shared Platform Knowledge reference | External to subtree | Green | Integration assumptions become harder to verify |\n| Shared Human Voice reference | External to subtree | Green | User-facing notification guidance becomes less explicit |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:dependencies -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:rollback -->\n## 7. ROLLBACK PLAN\n\n- **Trigger**: Validation errors increase or document structure drifts away from the active Level 3 template\n- **Procedure**: Revert the affected child documents and reapply the template-aligned structure while preserving valid Sales Ops content\n<!-- /ANCHOR:rollback -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:phase-deps -->\n## L2: PHASE DEPENDENCIES\n\n```\nParent shell ──► Phase 1 child bundle ──► Final validation\n```\n\n| Phase | Depends On | Blocks |\n|-------|------------|--------|\n| Parent shell | None | Child reference integrity |\n| Child bundle alignment | Parent shell | Final validation |\n| Final validation | All child documents | Completion |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:phase-deps -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:effort -->\n## L2: EFFORT ESTIMATION\n\n| Phase | Complexity | Estimated Effort |\n|-------|------------|------------------|\n| Setup | Medium | 1-2 hours |\n| Core Implementation | High | 2-4 hours |\n| Verification | Medium | 1-2 hours |\n| **Total** | | **4-8 hours** |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:effort -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:enhanced-rollback -->\n## L2: ENHANCED ROLLBACK\n\n### Pre-deployment Checklist\n- [ ] Previous valid revision identified\n- [ ] Affected documents isolated\n- [ ] Cross-links to parent shell preserved\n\n### Rollback Procedure\n1. Restore the last structurally valid document revision.\n2. Re-check anchors, headings, and level declarations.\n3. Run strict validation on the child folder.\n4. Run recursive validation on the parent folder.\n\n### Data Reversal\n- **Has data migrations?** No\n- **Reversal procedure**: N/A, documentation-only change set\n<!-- /ANCHOR:enhanced-rollback -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:dependency-graph -->\n## L3: DEPENDENCY GRAPH\n\n```\nspec.md ─────┐\n             ├──► plan.md ───► tasks.md\nchecklist.md ┤          └──► decision-record.md\n             └──► implementation-summary.md\n```\n\n### Dependency Matrix\n\n| Component | Depends On | Produces | Blocks |\n|-----------|------------|----------|--------|\n| spec.md | Parent shell | Requirements baseline | plan.md, tasks.md |\n| plan.md | spec.md | Execution strategy | tasks.md, checklist.md |\n| tasks.md | spec.md, plan.md | Task sequencing and AI protocol | Verification tracking |\n| checklist.md | spec.md, plan.md | Release-style validation | Final sign-off |\n| decision-record.md | spec.md, plan.md | Architecture rationale | Final review |\n| implementation-summary.md | All docs | Delivery recap | Completion claim |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:dependency-graph -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:critical-path -->\n## L3: CRITICAL PATH\n\n1. **Repair spec structure** - 30m - CRITICAL\n2. **Normalize plan, tasks, checklist, and summary** - 60m - CRITICAL\n3. **Consolidate ADRs and validation passes** - 45m - CRITICAL\n\n**Total Critical Path**: 2-3 hours\n\n**Parallel Opportunities**:\n- Checklist and decision-record drafting can proceed after the spec is stable.\n- Implementation summary can be finalized once validation outcomes are known.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:critical-path -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:milestones -->\n## L3: MILESTONES\n\n| Milestone | Description | Success Criteria | Target |\n|-----------|-------------|------------------|--------|\n| M1 | Structural alignment complete | Required headers and anchors restored | Phase 1 |\n| M2 | Sales Ops content normalized | Requirements, tasks, checklist, and ADRs match the template | Phase 2 |\n| M3 | Validation clean | Child and parent subtree report 0 errors | Phase 3 |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:milestones -->\n\n---\n\n## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD\n\n### ADR-001: Consolidate the initial Sales Ops package into one Level 3 phase bundle\n\n**Status**: Accepted\n\n**Context**: The initial Sales Ops package spans requirements, verification, and architecture choices that are too coupled for a Level 1 or Level 2 document set.\n\n**Decision**: Keep the initial creation work in a single Level 3 child phase with explicit parent references and validation gates.\n\n**Consequences**:\n- Reviewers can trace requirements, plan, tasks, checklist, and ADRs in one place.\n- The phase requires tighter structural discipline to satisfy Level 3 validation.\n\n**Alternatives Rejected**:\n- Split immediately into smaller child phases: rejected because the current work is still foundational and tightly coupled.\n\n### AI Execution Protocol\n\n#### Pre-Task Checklist\n1. Confirm `spec.md` scope has not changed.\n2. Identify the current phase in this plan.\n3. Verify task dependencies in `tasks.md`.\n4. Check relevant P0 and P1 items in `checklist.md`.\n5. Review the active ADR before changing structure.\n\n#### Execution Rules\n\n| Rule | Description |\n|------|-------------|\n| TASK-SEQ | Complete structural fixes before content refinements |\n| TASK-SCOPE | Stay inside the assigned subtree |\n| TASK-VERIFY | Re-run validation after each document update |\n| TASK-DOC | Keep cross-links synchronized |\n| TASK-STOP | Escalate if template alignment cannot be restored |\n\n#### Status Reporting Format\n\n```\nStatus: [IN_PROGRESS | COMPLETED | BLOCKED]\nDocument: [spec.md | plan.md | tasks.md | checklist.md | decision-record.md | implementation-summary.md]\nEvidence: [validation output or file path]\nNext: [next document or validation step]\n```\n\n#### Blocked Task Protocol\nIf a structural issue cannot be resolved in three attempts, stop editing the affected document, report the failing validator output, and preserve the last valid revision.\n\n---",

Canonical hook/runtime docs first, then package-level READMEs and supporting docs.\"\ntrigger_phrases:\n  - \"docs impact remediation plan\"\n  - \"026/009/012 plan\"\nimportance_tier: \"important\"\ncontextType: \"planning\"\n_memory:\n  continuity:\n    packet_pointer: \"system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/007-hook-parity/008-docs-impact-remediation\"\n    last_updated_at: \"2026-04-24T15:25:01Z\"\n    last_updated_by: \"backfill-memory-block\"\n    recent_action: \"Backfilled _memory block (repo-wide frontmatter sweep)\"\n    next_safe_action: \"Revalidate packet docs and update continuity on next save\"\n    key_files: [\"plan.md\"]\n---\n# Implementation Plan: Documentation Impact Remediation for 009 Hook/Daemon Parity\n\n<!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: 2 -->\n\n---\n\n## 1. APPROACH\n\nDocumentation-only phase. No code changes, no test harness, no schema migrations. Every edit must cite its driving sub-packet(s) from `../impact-analysis/merged-impact-report.md`. The merged report is the single source of truth for scope, severity, and flagging rationale — do not re-analyze sub-packets independently.\n\n### Guiding Principles\n\n1. **Truth over style.** A doc is updated only to the extent it is currently wrong or incomplete relative to shipped 009 behavior. Cosmetic polish is out of scope.\n2. **Evidence preserved.** Every change carries a pointer back to the flagging sub-packet (e.g. `[009/001]`) in commit messages or inline change notes.\n3. **Canonical-surface first.** `hook_system.md`, `SKILL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and top-level `AGENTS.md` are consumed by operator docs downstream. Update them first so per-package READMEs can cross-link to fresh text.\n4. **No scope creep.** If a file is accurate but could be improved, skip it. The impact analysis did not flag it — trust the analysis.\n5. **Reconcile Codex carefully.** Sub-packets diverge on whether Codex has a native lifecycle hook: 03 and 04 predate the native-SessionStart reconciliation landed in 05. `hook_system.md` and `SKILL.md` must describe the *post-05* state (native `SessionStart` gated by `codex_hooks` + `~/.codex/hooks.json`). Earlier packet summaries that still say \"Codex has no lifecycle hook\" are superseded.\n\n---\n\n## 2. PHASES\n\n### Phase 1 — Canonical Runtime Contracts (P0, sequential)\n\nGoal: make the upstream truth documents correct before any package/README touches them.\n\n1. **`references/config/hook_system.md`** (6 agents flagged — highest hotspot)\n   - Rewrite runtime matrix: add Claude `UserPromptSubmit`, update Codex row to native `SessionStart` + prompt hook gated by `codex_hooks`, describe OpenCode prompt-hook availability via the skill-advisor plugin + `experimental.chat.system.transform`, document Copilot file-based parity via `.claude/settings.local.json` top-level wrapper fields.\n   - Update cross-runtime fallback prose to match.\n   - Add or refresh the four-event `.claude/settings.local.json` example.\n\n2. **`AGENTS.md`** (repo root)\n   - Gate 2 rule: hook brief primary, `skill_advisor.py` fallback, cite hook reference.\n   - Runtime notes: Codex supports native `SessionStart` when `codex_hooks=true` and `~/.codex/hooks.json` wired.\n   - `sk-code-opencode` language table: note OpenCode plugin ESM exemption so `.opencode/plugins/` and `.opencode/plugin-helpers/` are excluded from the blanket `require`/`module.exports` rule.\n\n3. **`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/SKILL.md`**\n   - Startup/recovery section: split prompt-hook vs lifecycle-hook per runtime.\n   - Claude hook table: add `UserPromptSubmit` and clarify normalized four-event shape.\n   - Codex: describe native `SessionStart` + prompt hook when enabled, with `/spec_kit:resume` as fallback (post-05 state).\n   - Copilot: reference `.claude/settings.local.json` wrapper surface and writer wiring.\n\n4. **`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/ARCHITECTURE.md`**\n   - Copilot hook transport: describe `user-prompt-submit.ts`, `session-prime.ts`, `custom-instructions.ts` writing to `$HOME/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md`; hook stdout stays `{}`.\n   - OpenCode plugin bridge: describe ESM default-export entrypoint (`spec-kit-skill-advisor.js`), per-instance state isolation, in-flight identical-request dedup, cap/eviction semantics.\n\n### Phase 2 — Package-Level READMEs (P0, can parallelize)\n\n5. **`.opencode/README.md`** — Gate 2 prose, directory-structure pointers, advisor path corrected to `mcp_server/skill-advisor/`.\n\n6. **`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/README.md`** — hook-primary skill-advisor routing, `scripts/` ESM module profile (sub-packet 02's validator ESM flip), Copilot runtime-hooks summary, prompt-vs-lifecycle split.\n\n7. **`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/hooks/copilot/README.md`** (and any sibling runtime hook READMEs whose Copilot examples are stale) — replace `.github/hooks/scripts/*.sh` registration example with `.claude/settings.local.json` wrapper contract; clarify Claude nested commands remain alongside top-level Copilot fields.\n\n### Phase 3 — Install / Reference / Supporting Docs (P0 + P1)\n\n8. **`.opencode/install_guides/SET-UP - AGENTS.md`** — Gate 2 hook-first path, script fallback, native-tool/bootstrap verification, `--force-native` / `--force-local` / disable-flag notes.\n\n9. **`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/INSTALL_GUIDE.md`** — add `advisor_recommend` / `advisor_status` / `advisor_validate` to verification; Copilot row → merged `.claude/settings.local.json` wrapper execution + top-level field contract + writer wiring.\n\n10. **`feature_catalog/22--context-preservation-and-code-graph/05-cross-runtime-fallback.md`** — Copilot fallback entry named and describes top-level writer commands on `UserPromptSubmit` + `SessionStart`.\n\n### Phase 4 — MED Surfaces (P1, last)\n\n11. **`manual_testing_playbook/22--context-preservation-and-code-graph/252-cross-runtime-fallback.md`** — Copilot scenario expanded to inspect `.claude/settings.local.json` top-level fields/commands and smoke managed-block refresh.\n\n12. **`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/ENV_REFERENCE.md`** — add `SPECKIT_CODEX_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` entry.\n\n13. **`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/README.md`** — short hook-surface summary + cross-links.\n\n---\n\n## 3. DEPENDENCIES\n\n- **Upstream:** All 11 sibling sub-packets (001-011) implementation complete. Verified by merged impact report generation time (2026-04-23).\n- **Downstream:** None within this packet. External dependants (operator runbooks, onboarding guides) are out of scope.\n- **Parallel tracks:** Phase 2 files can be edited in parallel once Phase 1 lands, because they cross-link to Phase 1 text.\n\n---\n\n## 4. VERIFICATION STRATEGY\n\n1. **Per-file:** After each edit, verify the change addresses the specific reason recorded in the merged report for that path (not a related-but-different observation).\n2. **Cross-runtime consistency:** `hook_system.md`, `SKILL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `AGENTS.md` must agree on the post-05 Codex capability, the four-event Claude shape, the OpenCode plugin bridge transport, and the Copilot wrapper surface. Read them end-to-end before claiming Phase 1 done.\n3. **No stale references:**\n   - `grep -rn \"skill_advisor.py\" .opencode/README.md .opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/README.md AGENTS.md` should show only *fallback* references, never primary.\n   - `grep -rn \".github/hooks/scripts\" .opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/hooks/copilot/README.md` should be empty.\n   - `grep -rn \"CommonJS entrypoint.*plugin\" .opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/ARCHITECTURE.md` should be empty.\n4. **Validator:** `bash .opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/spec/validate.sh .opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/007-hook-parity/008-docs-impact-remediation/ --strict` must exit 0 or 1.\n5. **Parent graph metadata:** 009's `graph-metadata.json` must list 012 in `children_ids` after implementation.\n\n---\n\n## 5. EFFORT ESTIMATE\n\n- Phase 1 (4 files): ~120–180 LOC of edits. Mostly structural rewrites of small sections (matrix rows, startup paragraphs).\n- Phase 2 (3 files): ~60–100 LOC. Mostly prose + code-block example swaps.\n- Phase 3 (3 files): ~40–80 LOC. Verification-step additions + row updates.\n- Phase 4 (3 files): ~20–50 LOC. Additive only.\n\n**Total estimate:** ~240–410 LOC. Level 2 sizing (100-499).\n\n---\n\n## 6. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS\n\n- **Reviewability:** Every change must map 1:1 to a row in the merged impact report so reviewers can cross-check without re-running the 10 agents.\n- **Idempotence:** Edits should be safe to re-apply if a sub-packet reverts. No destructive deletes of content unrelated to the flagged reason.\n- **Anchor stability:** Do not rename or remove existing section anchors in the canonical docs; downstream tooling (memory indexer, validator) relies on stable anchors.\n\n---\n\n## 7. EDGE CASES\n\n- **Codex hook reconciliation conflict.** Sub-packets 03/04 say \"Codex has no lifecycle hook\"; sub-packet 05 ships native `SessionStart` parity. Resolution: document *post-05* state; earlier packet summaries remain in their own `implementation-summary.md` but do not leak into the canonical docs. Cross-check §2 Phase 1 tasks.\n- **Glob paths in impact report.** `feature_catalog/**`, `mcp_server/**/README.md`, and `manual_testing_playbook/**/*.md` resolve to specific target files identified in the underlying sub-packet reports; see merged report `Contributing Reasons` column for exact target names. Do not expand the glob literally — only touch the named targets.\n- **Duplicate reasons.** Some files were flagged by multiple sub-packets with partially overlapping reasons (e.g. `hook_system.md` by 6 sub-packets). Merge all reasons into one coherent rewrite; do not apply sequential edits that leave the doc inconsistent mid-phase.",

SUMMARY\n\n### Technical Context\n\n| Aspect | Value |\n|--------|-------|\n| **Language/Stack** | TypeScript, JavaScript, Markdown, JSON |\n| **Framework** | Vitest, Node.js, system-spec-kit validator |\n| **Storage** | Spec metadata JSON and packet-local markdown docs |\n| **Testing** | `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, targeted vitest, strict spec validation |\n\n### Overview\n\nThe remediation is ordered by review severity and dependency: first repair strict validation, then evidence traceability, then stale acceptance gates, then OpenCode runtime diagnostics, then continuity metadata. The implementation keeps code changes scoped to the plugin, bridge, and targeted vitest file while all documentation changes stay inside the 009 packet.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:summary -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:quality-gates -->\n## 2. QUALITY GATES\n\n### Definition of Ready\n\n- [x] Problem statement clear and scope documented in `spec.md`.\n- [x] User supplied the active spec folder and explicit write authority.\n- [x] Deep-review source and findings are identified in the parent review report.\n\n### Definition of Done\n\n- [ ] Phase 003 strict validation exits 0.\n- [ ] Parent and children 001/002/003 strict validation exits 0.\n- [ ] Typecheck, build, and targeted vitest command exit 0.\n- [ ] The parent remediation summary lists each finding with status, files, verification, and proposed commit message.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:quality-gates -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:architecture -->\n## 3. ARCHITECTURE\n\n### Pattern\n\nThin runtime adapter with explicit diagnostics.\n\n### Key Components\n\n- **OpenCode plugin transform**: parses bridge output and injects runtime code-graph context.\n- **OpenCode bridge**: invokes `session_resume` and serializes `opencodeTransport`.\n- **Phase 003 docs**: record requirements, decisions, tasks, checklist evidence, and validation state.\n- **Graph metadata**: exposes current packet status and file lineage to memory search.\n\n### Data Flow\n\n`session_resume` builds `data.opencodeTransport`; the bridge writes the handler JSON to stdout; the plugin parses stdout into a transport plan. When that parse fails or the transport plan is absent, the plugin or bridge must emit a visible diagnostic instead of silently returning the original system prompt.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:architecture -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:phases -->\n## 4. IMPLEMENTATION PHASES\n\n### Phase 1: Setup\n\n- [x] Read Phase 003 spec docs before editing.\n- [x] Run strict validation to capture current failures.\n- [x] Confirm stale command-doc reference source and allowed fix path.\n\n### Phase 2: Implementation\n\n- [x] Repair Phase 003 template headers and required anchors.\n- [x] Remove stale startup acceptance language that referenced a nonexistent Codex agent; retain `session_bootstrap` as the documented recovery path.\n- [ ] Add OpenCode plugin/bridge diagnostic behavior for absent or unparsable transport plans.\n- [ ] Add vitest coverage for the plugin diagnostic path.\n- [ ] Refresh continuity and graph metadata across parent plus children 001, 002, and 003.\n\n### Phase 3: Verification\n\n- [ ] Run typecheck.\n- [ ] Run build.\n- [ ] Run targeted vitest for OpenCode plugin and session resume.\n- [ ] Run strict validation on Phase 003, parent 009, child 001, and child 002.\n- [ ] Write final remediation summary.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:phases -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:testing -->\n## 5. TESTING STRATEGY\n\n| Test Type | Scope | Tools |\n|-----------|-------|-------|\n| Typecheck | MCP server TypeScript sources | `npm run typecheck` |\n| Build | MCP server compiled output | `npm run build` |\n| Unit/contract | OpenCode plugin, bridge, session resume | `vitest run tests/opencode-plugin.vitest.ts tests/session-resume.vitest.ts` |\n| Documentation | 009 parent and children | `validate.sh --strict --no-recursive` |\n\nTargeted vitest is the primary behavioral gate for this review because the requested finding is in the OpenCode plugin diagnostic path. Any broader baseline failures are recorded as deferred only when they are outside the authorized write scope.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:testing -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:dependencies -->\n## 6. DEPENDENCIES\n\n| Dependency | Type | Status | Impact if Blocked |\n|------------|------|--------|-------------------|\n| `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/spec/validate.sh` | Internal | Required | Cannot close traceability findings without strict validation exit 0. |\n| `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server` npm scripts | Internal | Required | Cannot verify code changes without typecheck/build/vitest. |\n| Existing 001/002 child docs | Internal | Required | Parent parity validation depends on child continuity staying coherent. |\n| Sandbox write authority | External | Constrained | Git staging/commit is forbidden; summary file hands off to orchestrator. |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:dependencies -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:rollback -->\n## 7. ROLLBACK PLAN\n\n- **Trigger**: Typecheck, build, targeted vitest, or strict validation remains red after scoped fixes.\n- **Procedure**: Do not run git reset. Document the blocker in the parent remediation summary, leave evidence-backed changes in place, and hand off a precise follow-up to the orchestrator.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:rollback -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:phase-deps -->\n## L2: PHASE DEPENDENCIES\n\n| Phase | Depends On | Blocks |\n|-------|------------|--------|\n| Phase 1 validation repair | Read current docs and validator output | Phase 2 evidence updates |\n| Phase 2 evidence updates | Phase 1 template compliance | Phase 3 startup gate cleanup |\n| Phase 3 startup gate cleanup | ADR-002 recovery decision | Phase 4 plugin diagnostics |\n| Phase 4 plugin diagnostics | Plugin and bridge reads | Phase 5 metadata refresh |\n| Phase 5 metadata refresh | Current validation and verification output | Phase 6 summary |\n| Phase 6 summary | All verification output | Orchestrator commit |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:phase-deps -->\n\n### AI Execution Protocol\n\n#### Pre-Task Checklist\n\n- Confirm the active spec folder and write authority.\n- Read every file before editing it.\n- Keep code edits scoped to the plugin, bridge, and targeted vitest file.\n\n#### Execution Rules\n\n| Rule | Requirement |\n|------|-------------|\n| TASK-SEQ | Follow the user-specified phase order. |\n| TASK-SCOPE | Do not edit files outside the authorized list. |\n| TASK-VERIFY | Run the requested verification commands after edits. |\n| TASK-TRUTH | Record failures as blocked or deferred with command output. |\n\n#### Status Reporting Format\n\nStatus Format: finding ID, status, files modified, verification output, and proposed commit message.\n\n#### Blocked Task Protocol\n\nIf a task is blocked by scope or sandbox constraints, mark it `DEFERRED` in the remediation summary and continue to the next safe in-scope phase.",
.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/013-embedder-testing-and-architecture/001-local-embeddings-foundation/017-llama-cpp-default-flip/scratch/probe-1k-corpus.json:3399:    "content": "---\ntitle: \"Implementation Summary [00--ai-systems/003-sales-process-automation/001-initial-creation/implementation-summary]\"\ndescription: \"Records how the Level 2 phase packet was repaired and validated.\"\ntrigger_phrases:\n  - \"implementation summary\"\n  - \"sales process automation summary\"\n  - \"initial creation summary\"\nimportance_tier: \"normal\"\ncontextType: \"general\"\ntemplate_source_hint: \"<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: impl-summary-core | v2.2 -->\"\n_memory:\n  continuity:\n    packet_pointer: \"00--ai-systems/003-sales-process-automation/001-initial-creation\"\n    last_updated_at: \"2026-04-24T15:25:01Z\"\n    last_updated_by: \"backfill-memory-block\"\n    recent_action: \"Backfilled _memory block (repo-wide frontmatter sweep)\"\n    next_safe_action: \"Revalidate packet docs and update continuity on next save\"\n    key_files: [\"implementation-summary.md\"]\n---\n# Implementation Summary\n\n<!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: 2 -->\n<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: impl-summary-core | v2.2 -->\n<!-- HVR_REFERENCE: .opencode/skill/sk-doc/references/hvr_rules.md -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:metadata -->\n## Metadata\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| **Spec Folder** | 001-initial-creation |\n| **Completed** | 2026-03-31 |\n| **Level** | 2 |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:metadata -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:what-built -->\n## What Was Built\n\nThe phase packet now validates as a proper Level 2 spec set instead of a collection of malformed long-form notes. You can review the System 7 HubSpot Sequences scope, plan, tasks, and checklist in the expected template order, which means the subtree can pass validation and serve as a stable reference again.\n\n### Level 2 Packet Repair\n\nThe repair kept the original System 7 intent, especially the command-driven sequence-design scope and STEPS quality framing, but moved that content into the required Spec Kit structure. That gives reviewers a predictable packet without losing the reason this phase exists.\n\n### Files Changed\n\n| File | Action | Purpose |\n|------|--------|---------|\n| `.opencode/specs/00--ai-systems-non-dev/003-sales-process-automation/001-initial-creation/spec.md` | Modified | Restored required Level 2 structure and preserved feature intent |\n| `.opencode/specs/00--ai-systems-non-dev/003-sales-process-automation/001-initial-creation/plan.md` | Modified | Replaced malformed sections with the template-aligned plan |\n| `.opencode/specs/00--ai-systems-non-dev/003-sales-process-automation/001-initial-creation/tasks.md` | Modified | Rebuilt the task list using the canonical three-phase scaffold |\n| `.opencode/specs/00--ai-systems-non-dev/003-sales-process-automation/001-initial-creation/checklist.md` | Modified | Added valid anchors, priority tags, and evidence-backed verification items |\n| `.opencode/specs/00--ai-systems-non-dev/003-sales-process-automation/001-initial-creation/implementation-summary.md` | Created | Added the missing required completion document |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:what-built -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:how-delivered -->\n## How It Was Delivered\n\nI repaired each markdown document against the canonical Level 2 templates, then ran the spec validator after every write until the child packet stopped reporting structural errors. The packet stayed documentation-only, so rollout was immediate once validation passed.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:how-delivered -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:decisions -->\n## Key Decisions\n\n| Decision | Why |\n|----------|-----|\n| Condense the original long-form System 7 notes into template sections | This preserved the feature intent while removing the malformed structure that broke validation |\n| Keep references limited to sibling docs and the parent `../spec.md` | Relative links inside the subtree are the safest way to satisfy integrity checks |\n| Add the implementation summary now instead of deferring it | Level 2 validation treats it as a required completion artifact once implementation work is documented |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:decisions -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:verification -->\n## Verification\n\n| Check | Result |\n|-------|--------|\n| Child folder validation | PASS, `validate.sh .opencode/specs/00--ai-systems-non-dev/003-sales-process-automation/001-initial-creation --verbose` reached 0 errors after repair |\n| Anchor and header review | PASS, required anchors and template headers now match across all Level 2 docs |\n| Link integrity review | PASS, broken markdown references were removed or replaced with valid sibling and parent links |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:verification -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:limitations -->\n## Known Limitations\n\n1. **Folder naming still reflects the parent workstream.** The content now clearly states that this phase documents the System 7 HubSpot Sequences packet, but the directory name remains `sales-process-automation`.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:limitations -->\n\n---",
.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/013-embedder-testing-and-architecture/001-local-embeddings-foundation/017-llama-cpp-default-flip/scratch/probe-1k-corpus.json:3599:    "content": "---\ntitle: \"Spec: sk-doc Legacy Template Debt Cleanup (Tier 4)\"\ntemplate_source: \"SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: spec-core | v2.2\"\ndescription: \"Address 93 HIGH + 177 MED findings from sk-doc template alignment audit on older spec folders. Pre-existing legacy debt; not regression-driven. Bulk fix via grouped pattern remediation.\"\ntrigger_phrases:\n  - \"008-sk-doc-legacy-template-debt-cleanup\"\n  - \"tier 4 legacy template cleanup\"\n  - \"sk-doc audit remediation\"\nimportance_tier: \"important\"\ncontextType: \"implementation\"\n_memory:\n  continuity:\n    packet_pointer: \"system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/000-release-cleanup/005-review-remediation/008-sk-doc-legacy-template-debt-cleanup\"\n    last_updated_at: \"2026-04-29T11:05:00Z\"\n    last_updated_by: \"claude-opus-4-7\"\n    recent_action: \"Completed eligible Tier 4 sk-doc template alignment cleanup\"\n    next_safe_action: \"Defer remaining prose-heavy MED issues to Tier 5\"\n    blockers: []\n    completion_pct: 100\n---\n\n<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: spec-core + level2-verify | v2.2 -->\n<!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: 2 -->\n\n# Spec: sk-doc Legacy Template Debt Cleanup\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:metadata -->\n## 1. METADATA\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| **Level** | 2 |\n| **Priority** | P2 |\n| **Status** | Complete |\n| **Created** | 2026-04-29 |\n| **Branch** | `main` |\n| **Parent** | `005-review-remediation` |\n| **Source** | sk-doc template alignment audit (`/tmp/audit-skdoc-alignment-report.md`) |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:metadata -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:problem -->\n## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE\n\n### Problem Statement\n\nThe sk-doc template alignment audit on the last 40 commits scanned 384 documentation files and surfaced **93 MISALIGN-HIGH + 177 MISALIGN-MEDIUM**. Most findings are pre-existing legacy debt: spec folders authored under earlier sk-doc template versions that never got upgraded to current frontmatter / anchor / template-source-marker requirements.\n\nThe 93 HIGH findings cluster into 15 pattern groups in the audit:\n\n- Groups 1, 2, 13-15: missing `_memory.continuity` frontmatter block (~33 files)\n- Groups 3-10: missing required anchors per template (`agents`, `commands`, `config`, `meta`, `readmes`, `scripts`, `skills`, `tests`, `when-to-use`, etc.) (~36 files)\n- Groups 11-12: missing `SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE` body marker (~2 files)\n\nMost affected folders:\n- `040-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-1/`\n- `041-sk-recursive-agent-loop/`\n- `042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/`\n- `022-hybrid-rag-fusion/001-hybrid-rag-fusion-epic/{...}`\n\nThese folders predate the current template surface. They produce strict-validator warnings but don't block production behavior; they hurt long-term maintainability.\n\n### Purpose\n\nBulk-fix the legacy debt by applying grouped pattern remediations:\n\n1. **_memory.continuity additions**: insert minimal valid block based on current packet state\n2. **Missing anchor additions**: insert template-aligned anchor stubs (with placeholder content if no real content exists)\n3. **TEMPLATE_SOURCE marker additions**: insert the body marker\n\nGoal: drop the audit's HIGH count from 93 → 0 and MED count from 177 → < 50 (pure legacy noise that can't be cleanly fixed without rewriting older docs).\n<!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:scope -->\n## 3. SCOPE\n\n### In Scope\n\n- All 93 MISALIGN-HIGH files in the audit report (`/tmp/audit-skdoc-alignment-report.md`)\n- The actionable subset of 177 MISALIGN-MEDIUM files (likely 80-100 fixable; rest require rewrites and become Tier 5+ deferred)\n- Grouped pattern fixes:\n  - Group 1+2+13-15: add `_memory.continuity` block to ~33 files\n  - Group 3-10: add missing anchors per the relevant template (~36 files)\n  - Group 11+12: add `SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE` body marker (~2 files)\n- Re-run sk-doc audit after batch; iterate if HIGH count > 0\n- Strict validator green on this packet\n\n### Out of Scope\n\n- Today's 9 packets (022-028 + 005/009 + 005/010): they're already aligned per their own validators\n- Files in scope of `006-stale-documentation-readme-fixes`: hand off to that packet\n- Files in scope of `007-vitest-broad-suite-honesty`: hand off\n- Top-level project README, license, contributor docs\n- `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `z_archive/`, `z_future/`\n- Rewriting legacy spec narrative (substantive content); only template-shape alignment\n- ALIGNED files\n\n### Approach: pattern-grouped batches\n\nDon't iterate file-by-file. Group by pattern:\n\n1. **Batch A — _memory.continuity additions**: identify all files missing `_memory.continuity`; for each, infer a minimal block from current state (packet folder name, last modified date, status) and insert before closing frontmatter `---`.\n2. **Batch B — anchor additions**: identify which anchors each file is missing (per category — spec, plan, tasks, etc.); for each anchor, insert a stub `ANCHOR:name` block with a section header and brief placeholder. If real content exists elsewhere in the file but isn't anchored, wrap it.\n3. **Batch C — TEMPLATE_SOURCE marker**: insert `<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: <inferred-template> | v2.2 -->` based on file type and location.\n\nAfter all 3 batches: re-run audit; iterate.\n\n### Files to Change (categories)\n\n| Category | Approx Count | Action |\n|---|---|---|\n| Files missing `_memory.continuity` | ~35 | Add block (Batch A) |\n| Files missing required anchors | ~40 | Add stubs (Batch B) |\n| Files missing TEMPLATE_SOURCE marker | ~5 | Add marker (Batch C) |\n| Misaligned-medium files | ~80-100 | Address opportunistically; remainder deferred |\n| Audit report (read-only reference) | 1 | `/tmp/audit-skdoc-alignment-report.md` |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:requirements -->\n## 4. REQUIREMENTS\n\n### P0 — Blockers (none)\n\n### P1 — Required\n\n| ID | Requirement | Acceptance Criteria |\n|----|-------------|---------------------|\n| REQ-001 | All MISALIGN-HIGH `_memory.continuity` findings resolved. | Re-run audit (or equivalent grep): 0 HIGH in Group 1, 2, 13-15. |\n| REQ-002 | All MISALIGN-HIGH missing-anchor findings resolved. | Re-run audit: 0 HIGH in Groups 3-10. |\n| REQ-003 | All MISALIGN-HIGH missing-TEMPLATE_SOURCE findings resolved. | Re-run audit: 0 HIGH in Groups 11-12. |\n| REQ-004 | MED count reduced. | Final MED count < 50 (or rationale documented for higher counts). |\n| REQ-005 | Strict validator green on this packet. | `validate.sh <packet> --strict` exits 0. |\n| REQ-006 | No regression in any of today's 9 packets. | Re-validate each: 028, 027, 026, 025, 024, 023, 022, 005/009, 005/010. All exit 0. |\n\n### Acceptance Scenarios\n\n1. **Given** the sk-doc audit re-runs after this packet, **when** the report's HIGH section is checked, **then** it has 0 entries (or only entries that were explicitly noted as deferred in implementation-summary).\n2. **Given** any of today's 9 packets is re-validated, **when** the strict validator runs, **then** it exits 0 (no regression introduced by Tier 4 cleanup).\n3. **Given** an audit finding points into a protected packet, **when** remediation scope is computed, **then** the file is excluded and documented rather than modified.\n4. **Given** a MED finding requires substantive narrative rewrite, **when** Batch D triages it, **then** it is deferred to Tier 5 with rationale.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n- **SC-001**: Re-run audit HIGH count = 0 (or fully documented if any deferred).\n- **SC-002**: MED count reduced.\n- **SC-003**: No regression in today's batch.\n- **SC-004**: Strict validator green.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:risks -->\n## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES\n\n| Type | Item | Mitigation |\n|------|------|------------|\n| Risk | Bulk anchor additions accidentally damage real content | Insert stubs ABOVE existing content, not in place; never delete |\n| Risk | _memory.continuity blocks become stale immediately | Use minimal valid blocks with `last_updated_at` = now and `next_safe_action: \"Refresh on next packet edit\"` |\n| Risk | Some legacy folders are intentionally minimal (e.g., archives) | Skip if path matches `z_archive/` or `z_future/` (already excluded) |\n| Risk | Regression in today's batch | REQ-006 enforces re-validation |\n| Dependency | sk-doc audit report at `/tmp/audit-skdoc-alignment-report.md` | Already produced today |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:nfr -->\n## L2: NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS\n\n### Performance\n- **NFR-P01**: Bulk operations should batch file writes to minimize tool-call overhead.\n\n### Reliability\n- **NFR-R01**: Every change must preserve the existing markdown content; only ADDITIVE changes (no deletions of substantive prose).\n- **NFR-R02**: After each batch (A, B, C), run a sanity grep to confirm no file became invalid.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:nfr -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:edge-cases -->\n## L2: EDGE CASES\n\n- A file is in scope but doesn't fit a template cleanly (e.g., a one-off note that got picked up by the audit): mark OUT-OF-SCOPE in implementation-summary; no edit.\n- A spec folder is mid-refactor or has parallel changes in another packet: skip with note.\n- A YAML frontmatter is malformed (parser failure): skip + flag as separate fix.\n- Some MED findings cannot be cleanly addressed without rewriting the file: defer to a future Tier 5 packet.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:edge-cases -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:complexity -->\n## L2: COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT\n\n| Dimension | Score | Notes |\n|-----------|-------|-------|\n| Scope | 18/25 | 130-200 files; broad cleanup |\n| Risk | 12/25 | Mostly additive; regression risk on today's batch managed via REQ-006 |\n| Research | 8/20 | Audit report is the playbook |\n| **Total** | **38/70** | **Level 2** |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:complexity -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:questions -->\n## 7. OPEN QUESTIONS\n\n- Q1: How many MED findings can realistically be closed in this packet vs deferred? **Default**: aim for 60-80%; document the rest as Tier 5 follow-up.\n- Q2: Should anchor stubs include real content or just empty placeholders? **Default**: empty placeholders with a `<!-- TODO: fill with real content -->` comment so future authors know to populate.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:questions -->",

The underlying spec content remains an analysis and planning artifact, so the summary records the current state without claiming deployment or completion work that has not happened.\n\n### Current Package State\n\nThe spec folder contains the analysis, plan, task breakdown, verification checklist, and ADR set for the anobel.com performance program. XCE claims ~20% token reduction with steering (F-043: external/README.md:188). Our system has zero per-session token measurement in its MCP server instrumentation layer (F-044): `prompt-cache.ts` is a cache with input-side token caps (lines 10-12), `budget-allocator.ts` is a pre-allocation planner (lines 52-117), `code-graph-context.ts` reports single-response `budgetUsed` via heuristic (line 199), and `compact-merger.ts` uses chars/4 estimation (lines 53-55). Actual session-level token counting EXISTS but OUTSIDE our MCP server — in `session-analytics-db.ts` (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens at lines 100-104; per-turn breakdown at lines 125-129) populated by `session-stop.ts` from LLM API usage envelopes (F-045). Measurement protocol: baseline-vs-after with N ≥ 10 sessions per condition, query `session-analytics-db.ts` `getSessionRow()` for `total_tokens` post-session-stop, compute paired delta (F-046). Verdict: ADAPT — measurement is deferrable to sub-packet 028 eval harness + 029 token instrumentation (~80 LOC total). Cannot ADOPT XCE's black-box methodology. Expected effect: 5-15% reduction (lower than XCE's 20% due to dynamic firing and different tool output format) (F-047).

That means it does not supply the missing shared `deep_loop_graph_*` bridge for research/review convergence (.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:294-300; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:9-10; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:21; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:50-67; .opencode/agents/agent-improver.md:175-177).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:319:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"Both deep-loop convergence contracts still document a reducer-owned in-memory graph bridge that is not present in the live reducer: deep research says \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the reducer builds an in-memory coverage graph\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" when `graphEvents` exist, and deep review says the same for review iterations (.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/references/convergence.md:1181-1205; .opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/convergence.md:658-683).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:711:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The published deep-research contract says that when `graphEvents` exist, \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the reducer builds an in-memory coverage graph and derives additional signals for the legal-stop gate evaluation,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" including graph coverage sub-checks (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/references/convergence.md:1181-1205`). The live research reducer does not implement that bridge: its only imports are `fs` and `path`, and its convergence score is taken from `latestIteration.convergenceSignals?.compositeStop` or `latestIteration?.newInfoRatio` rather than any graph helper (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:11-13`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:244-249`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1177:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The resume contract promises richer recovery than the shipped journal helpers provide. The skill says resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch, but the journal module only exposes raw-event readback, `getLastIteration()`, and `getSessionResult()`. If an interruption happens before a `session_ended` event is written, `getSessionResult()` returns `{ stopReason: null, sessionOutcome: null }`, so the helper surface itself does not reconstruct candidate, gate, benchmark, or trade-off state (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:290-300`, `.opencode/commands/deep/start-agent-improvement-loop.md:332-339`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/improvement-journal.cjs:148-203`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1263:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The published resume contract promises more reconstruction than the shipped recovery helper exposes. Both the command and skill say resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch, but the only recovery-facing journal helpers return the max iteration number and the terminal `stopReason/sessionOutcome`; there is no helper that rebuilds blocked-stop payloads, trade-off state, benchmark warnings, or lineage context from raw journal events (`.opencode/commands/deep/start-agent-improvement-loop.md:334-339`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:290-295`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/improvement-journal.cjs:168-203`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1530:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The shipped deep-review reducer mirrors the same pattern. `computeConvergenceScore()` reads `latest.convergenceSignals.compositeStop` or falls back to `1 - newFindingsRatio`, and the reducer then publishes only that scalar as `convergenceScore`. No inspected review reducer code reconstructs a coverage graph or invokes graph convergence logic before writing the dashboard/registry (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:360-390`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:579-583`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:671-680`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1551:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The standalone graph helper does have bounded weight, not runaway influence: `computeGraphConvergence()` builds `graphScore` from fragmentation (0.25), normalized depth (0.25), question coverage (0.30), and source diversity (0.20), then limits the merged result to `blendedScore = compositeStop * 0.6 + graphScore * 0.4`. Inside this helper, the coverage graph cannot contribute more than 40% of the final blended scalar (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/coverage-graph-convergence.cjs:141-205`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1735:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"A different namespace-isolation weakness does exist on the shared read side for research/review sessions: the convergence handler never accepts `sessionId`, constructs its namespace from only `{ specFolder, loopType }`, and then calls `getStats()` plus `computeSignals()` / `computeMomentum()` without session scoping, so convergence decisions aggregate all sessions sharing the same spec folder and loop type (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts:47-52`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts:92-111`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:511-545`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts:163-220`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1779:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The published `sk-improve-agent` contract and visible auto workflow keep that mutation coverage graph local to the improvement runtime rather than bridging it into the shared coverage-graph MCP. The skill describes `scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs` as the reader/writer for the coverage graph and says it uses `loop_type: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"improvement\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"` isolation, while the auto workflow only appends the state ledger and runs `scripts/reduce-state.cjs`; I found no visible `deep_loop_graph_upsert` step on this path (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:298-300`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:389-390`, `.opencode/commands/deep/assets/improve_agent-improver_auto.yaml:149-155`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1801:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The query surface only partially exposes session isolation. `handleCoverageGraphQuery()` accepts `sessionId` and passes it into `ns`, but the inspected helper queries for coverage gaps, contradictions, and unverified claims read by `spec_folder` and `loop_type` only, ignoring `ns.sessionId`; this means research/review sessions can be co-mingled on read even though improvement-mode entries are blocked from the DB entirely (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/query.ts:28-35`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/query.ts:55-58`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:63-126`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:136-147`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:238-277`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1823:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The shared SQLite coverage graph does not admit `improvement` loop types at all. The DB layer defines `LoopType = 'research' | 'review'`, constrains valid kinds/relations by those two namespaces, and the schema enforces `CHECK(loop_type IN ('research', 'review'))`; the MCP upsert handler repeats the same validation and rejects any other value (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:17`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:136-146`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:152-157`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/upsert.ts:51-53`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/upsert.ts:72-80`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:2121:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"`SKILL.md` says resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch and that the orchestrator skips mutation types already in the exhausted log, but the visible autonomous loop never invokes `mutation-coverage.cjs` before candidate generation. The shipped loop proceeds from integration scan directly to candidate generation, scoring, benchmarking, ledger append, reducer refresh, and reducer-driven stop check, so coverage state does not visibly steer mutation focus selection. (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:294-300`, Understand context before modifying. 2. **SCOPE LOCK:** Only modify files explicitly in scope. **NO** "cleaning up" or "improving" adjacent code. Scope in `spec.md` is FROZEN. 3. **VERIFY:** Syntax checks and tests **MUST** pass before claiming completion. **NO** blind commits. 4. **HALT:** Stop immediately if uncertain, if line numbers don't match, or if tests fail. (See "Halt Conditions" below). **OPERATIONAL MANDATES:** - **All file modifications require a spec folder** (Gate 3). - **Never lie or fabricate** - use "UNKNOWN" when uncertain. - **Clarify** if confidence < 80% (see §5 Confidence Framework). - **Use explicit uncertainty:** Prefix claims with "I'M UNCERTAIN ABOUT THIS:". **QUALITY PRINCIPLES:** - **Prefer simplicity**, reuse existing patterns, and cite evidence with sources - Solve only the stated problem; **avoid over-engineering** and premature optimization - **Verify with checks** (simplicity, performance, maintainability, scope) before making changes - **Truth over agreement** - correct user misconceptions with evidence; do not agree for conversational flow **HALT CONDITIONS (Stop and Report):** - [ ] Target file does not exist or line numbers don't match. - [ ] Syntax check or Tests fail after edit. - [ ] Merge conflicts encountered. - [ ] Edit tool reports "string not found". - [ ] Test/Production boundary is unclear. **MANDATORY TOOLS:** - **Spec Kit Memory MCP** for research tasks, context recovery, and finding prior work. **Memory saves MUST use `node.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/dist/memory/generate-context.js [spec-folder-path]`** - NEVER manually create memory files. **GIT WORKFLOW:** Full details: `.opencode/skills/sk-git/` - Worktree setup, conventional commits, PR creation, branch management - Trigger keywords: worktree, branch, commit, merge, pr, pull request, git workflow, finish work, integrate changes ### Quick Reference: Common Workflows | Task | Flow | | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **File modification** | Gate 3 (ask spec folder) → Gate 1 → Gate 2 → Load memory context → Execute | | **Research/exploration** | `memory_match_triggers()` → `memory_context()` (unified) OR `memory_search()` (targeted) → Document findings | | **Code search** | `Grep()` for text patterns, `Glob()` for file discovery, `Read()` for file contents | | **Resume prior work** | `/memory:continue` OR `memory_search({ query, specFolder, anchors: ['state', 'next-steps'] })` → Review checklist → Continue | | **Save context** | `/memory:save` OR `node.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/dist/memory/generate-context.js [spec-folder-path]` → Auto-indexed | | **Claim completion** | Validation runs automatically → Load `checklist.md` → Verify ALL items → Mark with evidence | | **End session** | `/spec_kit:handover` → Save context → Provide continuation prompt | | **New spec folder** | Option B (Gate 3) → Research via Task tool → Evidence-based plan → Approval → Implement | | **Complex multi-step** | Task tool → Decompose → Delegate → Synthesize | | **Documentation** | sk-doc skill → Classify → Load template → Fill → Validate (`validate_document.py`) → DQI score → Verify | | **Web code** | sk-code-web skill → Webflow/CDN standards, minification, browser testing | | **OpenCode system code** | sk-code-opencode skill → JS/TS/Python/Shell standards, language detection, quality checklists | | **Git workflow** | sk-git skill → Worktree setup / Commit / Finish (PR) | | **Phase workflow** | `/spec_kit:phase` → Decompose → `create.sh --phase` → Populate parent/children → `validate.sh --recursive` | | **Database maintenance** | `/memory:manage` → stats, health, cleanup, checkpoint, ingest operations | | **Analysis/evaluation** | `/memory:analyze` → preflight, postflight, causal graph, ablation, dashboard, history | ### Coding Analysis Lenses | Lens | Focus | Detection Questions | | ------------------ | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **CLARITY** | Simplicity | Is this the simplest code that solves the problem? Are abstractions earned? | | **SYSTEMS** | Dependencies | What does this change touch? What calls this? What are the side effects? | | **BIAS** | Wrong problem | Is user solving a symptom? Is this premature optimization? Is the framing correct? | | **SUSTAINABILITY** | Maintainability | Will future devs understand this? Is it self-documenting? Tech debt implications? | | **VALUE** | Actual impact | Does this change behavior or just refactor? Is it cosmetic or functional? | | **SCOPE** | Complexity match | Does solution complexity match problem size? Single-line fix or new abstraction? | ### Coding Anti-Patterns (Detect Silently) | Anti-Pattern | Trigger Phrases | Response | | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Over-engineering | "for flexibility", "future-proof", "might need" | Ask: "Is this solving a current problem or a hypothetical one?" | | Premature optimization | "could be slow", "might bottleneck" | Ask: "Has this been measured? What's the actual performance?" | | Cargo culting | "best practice", "always should" | Ask: "Does this pattern fit this specific case?" | | Gold-plating | "while we're here", "might as well" | Flag scope creep: "That's a separate change - shall I note it for later?" | | Wrong abstraction | "DRY this up" for 2 instances | "These look similar but might not be the same concept. Files called AGENTS.md commonly appear in many places inside a container - at "/", in "~", deep within git repositories, or in any other directory; their location is not limited to version-controlled folders. Their purpose is to pass along human guidance to you, the agent. Such guidance can include coding standards, explanations of the project layout, steps for building or testing, and even wording that must accompany a GitHub pull-request description produced by the agent; all of it is to be followed. Each AGENTS.md governs the entire directory that contains it and every child directory beneath that point. Whenever you change a file, you have to comply with every AGENTS.md whose scope covers that file. Naming conventions, stylistic rules and similar directives are restricted to the code that falls inside that scope unless the document explicitly states otherwise. When two AGENTS.md files disagree, the one located deeper in the directory structure overrides the higher-level file, while instructions given directly in the prompt by the system, developer, or user outrank any AGENTS.md content.   /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Opencode Env/Public zsh 2026-03-16 Europe/Amsterdam

This file is machine-owned and must stay synchronized with the latest iteration delta, dashboard metrics, and synthesized review report.

### Blocked-Stop and Corruption-Tracking Additions

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `blockedStopHistory` | array | One entry per `blocked_stop` JSONL event: `{run, blockedBy, gateResults, recoveryStrategy, timestamp}`. Rendered in the dashboard `BLOCKED STOPS` section and can drive the strategy `next-focus` anchor when blocked-stop is the most recent loop event. |
| `persistentSameSeverity` | array | Findings observed in ≥2 iterations with NO severity transitions beyond initial discovery. REQ-018 split of the deprecated `repeatedFindings` bucket. |
| `severityChanged` | array | Findings that went through at least one severity transition (P0↔P1↔P2) in their `transitions` history. |
| `repeatedFindings` | array | **Deprecated.** Union of `persistentSameSeverity` and `severityChanged`. Retained for backward compatibility, new code should read the split arrays. |
| `corruptionWarnings` | array | Per-line corruption reports from `parseJsonlDetailed()`: `{line, raw, error}`. Non-empty means the reducer detected malformed JSONL. |

### Default Values

When no `graph_convergence` event has been recorded yet, defaults are `graphConvergenceScore: 0`, `graphDecision: null`, and `graphBlockers: []`.
When no `blocked_stop` event has been recorded yet, `blockedStopHistory: []`.
When JSONL parses cleanly, `corruptionWarnings: []`.

### Fail-Closed Semantics (REQ-015, REQ-016)

- **Malformed JSONL**: The reducer CLI exits with code `2` and writes a warning to stderr when `corruptionWarnings.length > 0`. Pass `--lenient` (or `lenient:true` to `reduceReviewState`) to escape-hatch out and preserve the v1.2.0.0 fail-open behavior for legacy packets.
- **Missing machine-owned anchors**: `replaceAnchorSection()` throws `Error('Missing machine-owned anchor "<id>" in deep-review strategy file.')` when the strategy file is present but lacks one of the required anchors. Pass `--create-missing-anchors` (or `createMissingAnchors:true`) to bootstrap empty strategy files by appending the missing anchor blocks.
- **Dashboard surfaces**: `CORRUPTION WARNINGS` section lists detected lines. `BLOCKED STOPS` section lists `blockedStopHistory` entries. `GRAPH CONVERGENCE` section reports `graphConvergenceScore` / `graphDecision` / `graphBlockers`.
- **Strategy next-focus override**: When the latest `blocked_stop` event timestamp is newer than the latest iteration timestamp, the reducer rewrites the strategy `next-focus` anchor to surface the blocking gates and recovery hint so operators see the blocker before choosing the next iteration direction.

---


**Q: When should I use sk-doc vs. system-spec-kit?**

A: Use sk-doc for any task involving markdown quality, document creation (READMEs, install guides, catalogs, playbooks), or OpenCode component scaffolding (skills, agents, commands). Use system-spec-kit for spec folder lifecycle management: creating spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, checklist.md, and related spec folder documents. The two skills do not overlap. sk-doc must not write inside spec folders, and system-spec-kit does not handle DQI scoring, flowcharts, or component scaffolding.

**Q: Does `validate_document.py` check everything that `extract_structure.py` checks?**

A: No. They serve different purposes. `validate_document.py` is a fast format validator for README files specifically. It checks TOC presence, anchor format, H2 emoji rules, and required section presence. It exits 0 or 1. `extract_structure.py` is the full DQI analysis tool. It parses any markdown document type, produces a JSON report with three component scores, a checklist with pass/fail/skip per item, detected violations, and quality band. Use `validate_document.py` as a pre-delivery gate for READMEs and `extract_structure.py` for broader quality analysis and iteration tracking.
